subject: Clarifying keystore handover, escrow terms, and operator log access for private on-prem deployment
messages:
From: Samantha Li <samantha.li@gravemed.com>
To: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Tom Herrera <therrera@gravemed.com>, Bethany Cross <bethany.cross@gravemed.com>
Date: Fri, 10 May 2029 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Private deploy — keystore custody & operator access questions

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Before we move forward with procurement, legal and engineering have a few open items around the on-prem private deployment and key custody model. Can you confirm the following in writing so our InfoSec and legal teams can sign off?

1) If Gravemed elects customer-controlled keys (BYOK) for the private package, who holds the escrow copy of the keystore (Redwood, third-party escrow, or Gravemed-controlled HSM)?

2) In the event Redwood needs to perform emergency maintenance / break-glass, what access do your operators have to the keystore or decrypted material? Is access audited and restricted to named roles?

3) What logs or telemetry does Redwood collect from the private deployment’s control plane and operator activity? Are any logs containing plaintext model inputs/outputs or keys expected to leave Gravemed’s VPC?

We attach the current DPA draft and would like a short narrative that we can hand to our security reviewers. Appreciate a quick reply — our procurement target this month.

Best,
Samantha
Samantha Li
Head of Platform Security, Gravemed
From: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.inference.com>
To: Samantha Li <samantha.li@gravemed.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.inference.com>, irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Fri, 10 May 2029 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy — keystore custody & operator access questions

Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below; I’m looping in Kimberly (legal) and Irene (privacy/compliance) for the precise DPA/contract language and the attachments you requested.

1) Escrow / custody: Customer BYOK is supported. The default recommended pattern is Gravemed-controlled KMS/HSM (customer-managed) with an optional encrypted escrow held by a neutral third-party vault partner. Redwood does not retain plaintext key material in hosted or private BYOK setups. The term sheet (attached) describes escrow options and recovery procedures.

2) Operator access & break-glass: Redwood operators do not have access to customer key material when BYOK is enforced. Emergency break-glass can be supported only via an agreed playbook where Gravemed can grant time-limited access tokens or perform a hands-off recovery procedure. Any operator actions are logged and require multi-person approval; Kimberly — can you confirm the legal addendum we propose here?

3) Telemetry & logs: For private VPC/on-prem installs, the default is that no plaintext request/response content leaves the customer environment. Control-plane telemetry (health, metrics, error traces) is aggregated but sanitized. If a customer requests enhanced diagnostic logs that include request payloads, that would be an opt-in configuration with explicit contract language and retention limits. Irene — can you confirm retention windows we should propose to Gravemed?

I’ll follow up with a consolidated note and the suggested DPA addendum language.

Best,
Markus
Senior Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference
From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.inference.com>
To: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.inference.com>, irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Fri, 10 May 2029 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy — keystore custody & operator access questions

Markus — quick legal framing for Samantha’s team:

- DPA / Addendum: We propose a short addendum to the standard DPA that states: (a) customer retains ownership and control of cryptographic key material; (b) Redwood will not possess or derive plaintext keys; (c) Redwood’s access for maintenance is scoped to metadata and operational metrics only unless a signed break-glass request is executed per the agreed playbook.

- Escrow: We can include two escrow options: 1) customer-managed HSM with Redwood-held encrypted key-share at a neutral escrow vendor (recovery requires customer approval), or 2) customer chooses to keep all key material in their HSM with no escrow (higher recovery risk). We should include a clause about periodic escrow integrity checks if they pick option 1.

- Subprocessors: Any third-party escrow or diagnostic partner will be listed as a subprocessors appendix with limited subprocessing activities (escrow custody only; no access to runtime plaintext). We will commit to 30 days’ notice for material changes and a right-to-audit for large enterprise customers.

I’m attaching the DPA fragment and a short keystore term sheet for procurement to review. I recommend we propose a 90-day retention default for operator audit logs (redacted for payloads) and 7 days for any opt-in diagnostic payload logs unless Gravemed requests otherwise.

Kimberly
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.inference.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.inference.com>, irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Sat, 11 May 2029 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy — keystore custody & operator access questions

Thanks — one technical clarification for the addendum: when we say \"no plaintext keys\" we should be explicit about derived artifacts. Our runtime stores encrypted key-wrapping keys inside the customer tenancy but may cache wrapped key blobs in memory during live inference (never written to disk). We should call out that operator telemetry does not include in-memory dumps.

Also: break-glass flow options we can offer — 1) customer issues a time-limited grant token via their KMS and Redwood operators can run a scripted recovery without seeing the key; 2) escrow vendor performs key reconstruction only with two-person approval and a notarized request.

Irene — can you weigh in on the proposed retention numbers and whether we need any EU-specific language in case Gravemed processes EU patient data?

Markus
From: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.inference.com>
To: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.inference.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Sat, 11 May 2029 11:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy — keystore custody & operator access questions

Markus / Kimberly — agree with the language. A couple of compliance notes to include in the customer-facing addendum:

- Retention & jurisdiction: For US-only customers, the 90/7 default is fine. If Gravemed expects any EU patient data, we should add crossborder transfer language and limit any diagnostic payload transfers to EU-resident escrow or a fully anonymized subset.

- Audit evidence: Offer to provide redacted operator audit logs and notarized escrow integrity proofs as part of the security pack. Document must reference SOC2-type evidence for subprocessors.

- Emergency access notification: We should require near-real-time notification to the customer’s security contact when break-glass is used, and a post-incident report within 48 hours.

I’ve added suggested sentence-level wording for the addendum in the attached term-sheet.

Irene
Senior Privacy & Compliance Manager
From: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.inference.com>
To: Samantha Li <samantha.li@gravemed.com>, Tom Herrera <therrera@gravemed.com>
Cc: Bethany Cross <bethany.cross@gravemed.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.inference.com>, irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Sun, 12 May 2029 17:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy — keystore custody & operator access questions

Hi Samantha / Tom — thanks for the patience. Attached are three items for your review: (1) an annotated DPA addendum (Gravemed-DPA-draft-v3.pdf) that includes the BYOK/escrow options and break-glass playbook language; (2) a keystore-escrow-term-sheet.docx that lists operational steps for both escrow options; and (3) operator-access-matrix.xlsx showing which roles can request diagnostics, what approvals are required, and default retention windows.

Summary (short bullets for your security team):
- Custody: Gravemed keeps primary control. Redwood will not possess plaintext key material in BYOK configurations.
- Escrow: Optional encrypted escrow at a neutral vendor (recovery with customer approval) or no-escrow option.
- Operator access: No direct access to keys; break-glass only on signed/time-limited approval flows. Operator actions are multi-person approved and logged.
- Logs & telemetry: Control-plane metrics and sanitized traces are collected. Plaintext payloads are never exfiltrated by default; opt-in diagnostics that include payloads are contractually limited and timeboxed.
- Compliance: Offer SOC2 evidence for subprocessors, 90/7 default retention for redacted operator logs / payloads respectively, and 48-hour post-incident reporting for any emergency access.

Next steps: If this aligns with Gravemed’s requirements, Kimberly will produce a DPA addendum for signature and we can attach the DocuSign envelope for the escrow addendum if you choose option 1. Link to the DocuSign and shared Drive folder is included above.

Happy to hop on a 30-minute call if your security or procurement team prefers to walk through the playbook.

Best,
Markus
Senior Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Gravemed-DPA-draft-v3.pdf (DPA fragment), keystore-escrow-term-sheet.docx (term sheet), operator-access-matrix.xlsx (role matrix)
